notes: Biggest skill effect is on process and organisation, not raw model quality: every baseline run skipped collections/descriptive names (failed in 4/4) and 2/4 skipped any QA pass, while all skill runs did both.
Mug is the most discriminating case (14/14 vs 10/14): baseline left flat roughness on the hero glaze, no QA, and did not frame its choices as assumptions.

Non-discriminating assertions: render engine/AgX, render file exists, materials assigned, Roman numerals scale, hydrant height, rails/track parts - both configurations pass them every time. Visual quality differences (hydrant scene depth, watch inscription) are better judged in the Outputs tab than by these checks.
Station case ties at 10/11: both runs built a shortened platform (51 m and 57 m vs ~110-130 m real). The skill version now explicitly says to keep full length via instancing and to flag any shortcut.
Watch with-skill 'failure' on twelve numerals is debatable: it omitted VI for the sub-seconds dial, which is period-correct. Consider rewording that assertion.
Cost: skill runs took ~2-3x longer and ~1.6-2x the tokens (e.g. watch 19 min vs 7 min), spent on test-render iterations and the audit pass.

Caveats: the station runs were built headless because the live Blender MCP connection dropped; the station baseline was interrupted by a usage limit and resumed, so its timing covers only the resumed part. Hydrant with-skill may have read partly-updated skill files mid-run. Mug/hydrant baselines and later runs used a snapshot of the original skill (skill-snapshot-v1); the station with-skill run used the updated skill.
